entry_points.summary: Collect commands, agents, and skills from repo root into kind-keyed dict
Require Supported, Unsupported, and Notes sections in CAPABILITIES.md
Compute conventional output path for target, kind, and id
Replace Agent/Skill/tool-schema call sites with Cursor limitation comment
Render one source entry as a Cursor .mdc rule with YAML frontmatter
Build command-ID set, emit and validate Cursor .mdc rules, append -skill suffix on collision
Replace unsupported call sites with Codex limitation comment
Render command or skill as Codex prompt with # /<id> header
Consolidate all agents into single AGENTS.md
Build command-ID set, emit Codex prompts and AGENTS.md, append -skill suffix on collision
Replace unsupported call sites with Antigravity limitation comment
Render command as Antigravity workflow .md (description frontmatter, 250-char limit)
Render agent as Antigravity rule .md with always_on or model_decision trigger
Render skill as Antigravity SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter
Render flat agy prompt with description and role frontmatter
Generate agy-plugin.yaml export manifest (z-harness convention only)
Emit and validate all agy surfaces: workflows, rules, skills, prompts, manifest, caps, README
Exit 1 immediately when forbidden tarball pattern is matched
Search tarball listing for one forbidden pattern (fixed-string or regex)
Parse --target, run adapters sequentially, report OK/FAILED per target

invariants: Source of truth is commands/, agents/, and skills/*/SKILL.md — never the exports/ tree
Unsupported constructs are replaced line-by-line with explicit limitation comments, never silently dropped
Each adapter validates all emitted files before reporting success
CAPABILITIES.md must contain ## Supported, ## Unsupported, and ## Notes sections
/z-export runs adapters sequentially and continues past individual target failures
audit-tarball.sh rejects providers.json, .z-harness/, plan artifacts, exports/, and absolute home paths
When a skill ID collides with a command ID, both Cursor and Codex adapters append a -skill suffix to the export filename to prevent overwrite
gotchas: Skill/command ID collision handling: if a skill and a command share the same ID, the skill's export filename gets a -skill suffix (e.g. z-plan-skill.mdc) in both Cursor and Codex adapters
export-common.py does not enforce tarball exclusions; that gate lives in audit-tarball.sh
Codex consolidates all agents into AGENTS.md — no per-agent prompt files are emitted
agy emits the most surfaces: workflows + rules + skills + flat prompts + manifest + CAPABILITIES.md + README.md
agy _ALWAYS_ON_AGENTS hard-codes implementer, reviewer, auditor, mr-reviewer, remote-runner; all others get model_decision
agy-plugin.yaml is a z-harness convention manifest; Antigravity does not read it natively
Antigravity workflow bodies have an ~12,000 character limit; several z-harness commands exceed it
export-common.py is loaded via importlib in each adapter because the hyphen prevents direct Python import
